status: NEW (Roman, 2026-09-20) — real Attempt 8 correction. Every real generation of First Sacrifice's Scene 1 wish-twist beat (attempts 4 through 8) independently converged on the SAME wrong visual grammar: a dark seam/rift, a twisting rope of light, a directed magical attack, scorch-mark residue cited as evidence. That convergence traces directly to this packet's own instructions ("a concrete FORCE... a real, immediate physical/magical threat aimed at Lirael", "grounded in visible residue the assembly just witnessed") — the model was doing exactly what it was told. Roman's correction: an ORDINARY misaligned wish is not a magical attack. This is now a SHARED FATELANDS LAW, not a First-Sacrifice-only fix, because the same instruction-shape ("make the magic concrete/visible/threatening") will recur in any Fatelands Fantasy story with a wish that bends — the wrongness is structural to how 'concrete' was specified, not particular to this one scene.

scope.applies_to: Fatelands Fantasy — ORDINARY wish misalignment only (a single character's wish bending away from its stated intent, the everyday texture of Fatelands magic).
scope.explicitly_distinct_from: Major, world-scale Fatelands phenomena — The Fold and The Staircase — which are large-scale reality-seam events with their own established, separately-canonical visual language (see project_fatelands_fold_ontology, project_fatelands_ascendant_staircase). This law does NOT govern those; it governs the far more common case of one person's wish going wrong in an ordinary social/dramatic moment.
explicitly_excluded: Famous Fate worlds (independently canonical, this law never applies)
scope.gate_contract: Runtime: _fatelandsFantasyWorldGate() in public/app.js (state.picks.world === 'Fantasy' && state.fateMode !== 'famous_fate') — the same real gate every other Fatelands-conditional directive in this codebase uses. Authoring-packet: packet.world_scope === 'fatelands_fantasy', enforced by a throw in _first_sacrifice_authoring_adapter.mjs if a packet citing this law is not scoped correctly.

statement: An ordinary misaligned Fatelands wish does not manifest as a visible external attack. It manifests as a SUBJECTIVE experience for the person it targets: recognition of the wrongness taking shape, an inward pull toward an unwanted or dangerous fulfillment, and — if the misfire is checked — an unexplained cessation with no flare, no spectacle, no visible rescuer, and no mechanism the viewpoint character can name. The magic is real and the stakes are real; the VISUAL GRAMMAR is internal and dreadful, never a projectile, a rift, or a blast.
why: A wish is an intention bending in the world, not a weapon being fired. Depicting misalignment as a physical attack (a beam, a seam, a burst) turns an intimate, character-driven wrongness into a generic action-magic effect — it also manufactures a physical event (residue, scorch, damage) that then gets cited as 'evidence' in a way that makes the surrounding social/legal drama (a public charge grounded in what people actually felt/recognized, not in forensic damage) read as an afterthought to a fight scene that never needed to happen.

valid_for_ordinary_wish_misalignment.description: An inward, subjective sense of being drawn toward something — felt as directionality or dread, never as an external force with a visible trajectory or point of origin.

The viewpoint character's own dawning understanding that the wish is resolving wrongly, grounded in what was just said/seen (a person's words, gaze, behavior) — a cognitive/emotional beat, not a special effect.

A deliberately unclear sense that something has shifted, is about to happen, or is already underway — the character (and reader) cannot yet name it. Never resolves into a described object, ray, or shape moving through space.
The felt pull or dread simply stops. No visible mechanism, no rescuer shown or implied, no explanation offered to the viewpoint character or the reader in that moment.

invalid_for_ordinary_wish_misalignment.description: Any directed magical bolt, beam, rope, seam, or blade of energy moving toward a target — the visual grammar of a weapon being fired, not a wish bending.
A literal tear, rift, or seam opening in the air or in reality.
Bursts, blasts, flares, or other visible releases of magical force.

Scorch marks, burn lines, flattened/singed ground, or any other physical damage cited afterward as evidence of what happened — manufactures forensic 'proof' an ordinary wish misalignment does not produce.

effect_classification.boundary_note: This classification governs ORDINARY wish misalignment only. It says nothing about how The Fold, The Staircase, or other major world-scale phenomena may look — those are separately canonical and explicitly out of scope here (see scope.explicitly_distinct_from).

first_sacrifice_application.note: First Sacrifice Scene 1's wish-twist/arrest beats are the real case that surfaced this law. The packet's scene1_causal_sequence, wish_twist_and_arrest_requirement, required_content_beats, and scene1_beat_number_template have been corrected to require the quiet-misalignment shape (recognition -> pull -> unexplained arrest) and to explicitly forbid the attack-grammar vocabulary. See _first_sacrifice_source_packet.json's wish_twist_and_arrest_requirement.governing_law field (same governing_law citation shape as scene1_answer_manifestation.governing_law) for the exact pointer.

implementation_status.real_runtime_source_of_truth: public/app.js — buildFatelandsOrdinaryWishMisalignmentDirective(), a static (stateless) directive gated on _fatelandsFantasyWorldGate(), wired into the same 3 literary directive-stack call sites and 1 CG call site as buildFatelandsManifestationLawDirective.
implementation_status.eligibility_vs_consumption: Unlike the manifestation ledger, this law needs no per-story registered state — it is a standing rule for ANY ordinary wish-misalignment content in ANY Fatelands Fantasy story, so it renders unconditionally (subject only to the world gate) rather than being relevance-gated to specific entities.
implementation_status.first_sacrifice_note: First Sacrifice's packet-level citation (wish_misalignment_governing_law) and the real runtime directive are two separate consumers, same as the manifestation law's own disclosed pattern — the packet documents the requirement for this one scene's authoring pass; the runtime directive is what reaches an ordinary (non-baked) Fatelands Fantasy story's live author/CG context.
